instructions:
This server bridges development tasks to the local DSH (DeepSeek Harness) headless runner.
- dsh_env: inspect the environment first (versions, CLI path, token, ready-made codex config).
- dsh_run: start a fresh DSH session for a task. State the goal, constraints and acceptance command; DSH reads/writes files and runs commands itself. Pass the project root as cwd.
- dsh_resume: continue the session returned by dsh_run; reuse the same cwd.
- Success means: final event present, turn_end=completed, exit code 0. Otherwise the tool result carries isError plus diagnostics.
- Verify the delivered work independently (for example `node --test test\*.test.mjs`); do not treat DSH's own summary as acceptance.

dsh_env.title: DSH environment check
dsh_env.description: Returns plugin version, MCP URL and token, DSH CLI path and version, profile, DSH_HOME, permission mode, node runtime, default timeout and concurrency limit, plus a [mcp_servers.dsh_codex] block ready to paste into Codex config.toml. Read-only; starts no task.

dsh_run.title: Run a task with DSH (new session)
dsh_run.description: Starts a fresh DSH headless session in the given working directory and returns the final answer, session id, exit code, turn_end, token usage and a resume hint. DSH really edits files and runs commands. On failure (timeout, non-zero exit, empty answer, turn_end not completed) the result is marked isError and includes the stderr tail and event counts.
dsh_run.task: Task description for DSH. Include the goal, constraints (e.g. "Node built-ins only", "do not touch other files") and how to verify. The text is piped verbatim to DSH's stdin.
dsh_run.cwd: Working directory (project root) for the task; must be an existing absolute path. Defaults to the plugin's defaultCwd.
dsh_run.timeout_sec: Timeout in seconds. Defaults to the plugin's defaultTimeoutSec (3600). A timeout kills the whole process tree.

dsh_resume.title: Resume an existing DSH session
dsh_resume.description: Continues an existing session (its context is kept) and returns the new final answer and usage. cwd must match the one the session was created with, otherwise DSH refuses.
dsh_resume.session_id: Session id returned by a previous dsh_run/dsh_resume call (e.g. session-xxxxxxxx-...).

common.include_events: Attach the tail of DSH's NDJSON event stream to the result (summary only by default; enable when debugging).
